newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO supported by local buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO supported by local buying interest.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday edged higher on buying interest from a local trader seeking to mop up any cheap offers, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil prices were bid/asked at $120/$121 per tonne, unchanged from Tuesday despite sharply weaker crude prices. An offer was last seen at $121.50 for end-December loading supplies.
Traders said a local trader's emergence to buy from a major oil company on Tuesday was indicative that the buyer would likely be a keen buyer for the rest of the week.
They said physical fundamentals is healthy. Chinese demand continued to prop up prices, traders said.
"Chinese buying will continue until stocks within the country is sufficient to tide over the one-week festive Chinese Lunar New Year," said a trader.
In the swaps market, December was up at $120.25/$121.00, lower from Tuesday's quotes of $119.75/$120.75 despite crude losses. Traders said this is evident that the physical market is not that weak.
